description: Roman-era and Brittonic forms (Londinium, Eboracum, Camulodunum) aren't in our current corpus — Skeat/Mawer all start at Anglo-Saxon. Holder's Alt-celtischer Sprachschatz (1896) is public domain and covers the Celtic/Roman strata. Needed to make the Londinium→London chain work end-to-end. Three volumes on archive.org. Format is dense and German, would need a different parser than Skeat.
notes:
Adding more PD Celtic/Brittonic source candidates per Claude-twin feedback:
- Sir John Rhys, multiple works on Welsh / Brittonic toponymy (late 1800s, PD)
- Melville Richards' archive / Welsh place-name studies (some PD)
- Geiriadur Prifysgol Cymru — older fascicles' source material is largely PD even though the dictionary itself has copyright complications

These layered with Holder's Alt-celtischer Sprachschatz give a deeper 'elder-tongue' register that predates Modern Welsh — useful for elven settings wanting more archaic feel.

title: Time-aware generator: render same etymon in multiple historical strata
description:
Same etymological breakdown (bere + tun) should render in any chosen period: OE 'bere-tūn' → ME 'Bertune' → 'Bartone' (Domesday) → 'Barton' (modern). Atmospheric for fantasy gaming — 'what was this town called in 800 AD?'

Building blocks:
1. Ingest dated attestations from the etymology corpus into toponym_attestation (Skeat/Mawer/Ekwall list these religiously). LLM extractor needs an attestations: [{form, year, source_doc}] field added to its response schema.
2. New table etymon_period_form (or a date_range column on reflex) so the SAME etymon carries its surface variants across periods, not just per-toponym.
3. Period taxonomy — coarse first: 'old-english' (pre-1066), 'middle-english' (1066-1500), 'early-modern' (1500-1700), 'modern' (1700+). Fine-grained later if useful.
4. Generator gains a 'period' or 'era' input parameter. For an unattested compound, derive the period-specific form by looking up each etymon's surface variants for that period. Where multiple variants attested, sample weighted.
5. For periods where an etymon has no attestation, optionally fall back to phonological rules (OE -tūn → ME -tun → -tone → -ton) — but this is much later work; coverage from attestations should be high.

The toponym_attestation table is the raw input to (2). For etymon-level period forms we'd also want to mine the variant historical spellings the books print throughout each entry.

Pairs naturally with the historical-vs-modern register knob we already discussed (currently just 'register: modern' as the default).

title: Build alphabetical-dictionary parser for non-Skeat books
description: Mawer, Ekwall, Johnston, Joyce, Watson — all in alphabetical-entry format rather than Skeat's TOC+suffix-section format. Current parser returns 0 entries on these. Need a generic alphabetical parser: detect headword (capitalized at paragraph start), extract entry body up to next headword. Then feed to the same LLM extractor. Covers the remaining 27 books in sources/.
notes:
Starting work — pilot on Mawer Northumberland-Durham 1920 first, then test against Ekwall and Johnston for format coverage.
Phase 1 done: pilot on Mawer Northumberland-Durham succeeded. Parser handles Skeat-format AND alphabetical-dictionary format with auto-detection. Working well on: Mawer NorthDur (838 entries), Ekwall Lancs (499), Duignan Staffs (337), Harrison Liverpool (215), Watson Ross (652), Watson Celtic (474), Joyce vol 3 (606), Morgans (~830), Macbain (178), Gillies Argyll (155).

Still problematic (deferred):
- Taylor 1893: parser grabs back-of-book index entries (toponym + page number, no etymology body). Needs back-matter / index detection.
- Joyce vol 1: thematic chapters not alphabetical — wrong shape entirely. Skip; vol 3 is the dictionary.
- Lindkvist, Wyld/Hirst, Mawer 1922/1924/Stenton: small/methodological volumes with mixed content — low yield expected.
- Watson 1926 has some 3-letter false-positive headwords leaking through (Ady, Ann, Arch, Bede).

title: Sonnet/Haiku second pass for low-confidence LLM extractions
description: Qwen 9B leaks modern forms ('king' instead of 'cyning', 'mill' instead of 'myln', 'town' instead of 'tun') on some entries, and misreads attestation fragments as etymons (Croxton: 'estone'). Add a review CLI that picks toponym_etymology rows with confidence in (medium, low) and notes containing 'extracted_by:llm:qwen', re-runs them via the Anthropic API (Haiku first, Sonnet for residue), and inserts new rows from the better extractor. Old rows stay; consensus view shows where they agree/disagree.
notes:
Pivot to Gemini for second-pass review — user has GEMINI_API_KEY configured but no Anthropic key. Less bureaucratic: free-tier covers expected volume, paid pricing for 2.5-flash is very cheap (~$0.075/M input). Will build as a parallel client to OllamaClient with the same extract_one signature, then add --provider {ollama|gemini} flag on mine-llm.
Implemented as 'wyrd kenning lexicon review <source_dir>' command. Dry-runs by default; --apply to insert new toponym_etymology rows tagged with extracted_by:gemini:<model>. Idempotent — skips toponyms that already have a Gemini row. Filters by --book / --confidence / --limit. Tested end-to-end against the in-progress DB (3 Cambridgeshire entries, ~36s for 3 calls).
